   135	// A git execFile whose HEAD is chosen per rev-parse-HEAD call (the drift seam),
   136	// and which counts those calls so a test can pin the exact number of
   137	// prepare->commit windows. gitSnapshot reads clean status/diffs.
   138	function gitExec(headForCall) {
   139	  let headCalls = 0;
   140	  const fn = (/** @type {string} */ cmd, /** @type {string[]} */ args = []) => {
   141	    if (cmd !== 'git') return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('spawn ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }));
   142	    const key = args.join(' ');
   143	    if (key === 'rev-parse HEAD') {
   144	      headCalls += 1;
   145	      return Promise.resolve({ stdout: headForCall(headCalls) + '\n', stderr: '' });
   146	    }
   147	    const out = key === 'rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD' ? 'main' : '';
   148	    return Promise.resolve({ stdout: out + '\n', stderr: '' });
   149	  };
   150	  fn.headCalls = () => headCalls;
   151	  return fn;
   152	}

   154	// Spy every write touching .handoff/loop.
   155	function spyLoopWrites(io) {
   156	  const writes = /** @type {string[]} */ ([]);
   157	  const note = (/** @type {any} */ p) => { if (typeof p === 'string' && p.startsWith('/repo/.handoff/loop')) writes.push(p); };
   158	  for (const m of ['writeFileSync', 'appendFileSync', 'mkdirSync', 'unlinkSync', 'rmSync']) {
   159	    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
   160	    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ p, /** @type {any} */ a) => { note(p); return real(p, a); };
   161	  }
   162	  for (const m of ['renameSync', 'copyFileSync']) {
   163	    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
   164	    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ from, /** @type {any} */ to) => { note(from); note(to); return real(from, to); };
   165	  }
   166	  return writes;
   167	}

   171	   121	function gitExec(headRef) {
   172	   122	  return (/** @type {string} */ cmd, /** @type {string[]} */ args = []) => {
   173	   123	    if (cmd !== 'git') return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('spawn ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }));
   174	   124	    const key = args.join(' ');
   175	   125	    const out = key === 'rev-parse HEAD' ? headRef() : key === 'rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD' ? 'main' : '';
   176	   126	    return Promise.resolve({ stdout: out + '\n', stderr: '' });
   177	   127	  };
   178	   128	}

   181	   131	function spyLoopWrites(io) {
   182	   132	  const writes = /** @type {string[]} */ ([]);
   183	   133	  const note = (/** @type {any} */ p) => { if (typeof p === 'string' && p.startsWith('/repo/.handoff/loop')) writes.push(p); };
   184	   134	  for (const m of ['writeFileSync', 'appendFileSync', 'mkdirSync', 'unlinkSync', 'rmSync']) {
   185	   135	    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
   186	   136	    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ p, /** @type {any} */ a) => { note(p); return real(p, a); };
   187	   137	  }
   188	   138	  for (const m of ['renameSync', 'copyFileSync']) {
   189	   139	    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
   190	   140	    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ from, /** @type {any} */ to) => { note(from); note(to); return real(from, to); };
   191	   141	  }
   192	   142	  return writes;
   193	   143	}

     1	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
     2	
     3	// Git facts degrade to null rather than block a checkpoint: not-a-repo,
     4	// missing binary, and timeouts are all expected environments (plan §Root
     5	// discovery & degraded modes).
     6	const GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000;
     7	// The untracked digest is bounded: beyond this many paths, entries fold in by
     8	// name only, keeping prepare-time hashing cheap on huge untracked trees.
     9	const UNTRACKED_CAP = 200;
    10	// NUL separator: cannot occur in diffs, sizes, hex hashes, or file paths, so
    11	// joined digest inputs cannot collide across field boundaries.
    12	const SEP = String.fromCharCode(0);
    13	const NEWLINE = String.fromCharCode(10);
    14	
    15	const sha256 = (/** @type {string} */ s) => createHash('sha256').update(s).digest('hex');
    16	
    17	/**
    18	 * Capture the repo's git state plus a content-sensitive digest. The digest
    19	 * covers the staged diff, unstaged diff, and a bounded untracked-files digest
    20	 * (path + size + content hash) — NOT the HEAD sha, which the receive token
    21	 * binds as its own input, so a HEAD-only move is distinguishable from a
    22	 * content change.
    23	 * @param {{execFile: Function, cwd: string, fs: any}} deps
    24	 * @returns {Promise<{branch: string, headSha: string, dirty: boolean, dirtySummary: string[], contentDigest: string} | null>}
    25	 */
    26	export async function snapshot({ execFile, cwd, fs }) {
    27	  const git = (/** @type {string[]} */ args) => execFile('git', args, { cwd, timeout: GIT_TIMEOUT_MS });
    28	  let branch, head, status, staged, unstaged, untrackedList;
    29	  try {
    30	    [branch, head, status, staged, unstaged, untrackedList] = await Promise.all([
    31	      git(['rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD']),
    32	      git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD']),
    33	      git(['status', '--porcelain']),
    34	      git(['diff', '--cached']),
    35	      git(['diff']),
    36	      git(['ls-files', '--others', '--exclude-standard']),
    37	    ]);
    38	  } catch {
    39	    return null;
    40	  }
    41	
    42	  const nonEmptyLines = (/** @type {string} */ s) => s.split(NEWLINE).filter((/** @type {string} */ l) => l !== '');
    43	  const dirtySummary = nonEmptyLines(status.stdout);
    44	  const untrackedPaths = nonEmptyLines(untrackedList.stdout);
    45	
    46	  const untrackedEntries = untrackedPaths.map((rel, i) => {
    47	    if (i >= UNTRACKED_CAP) return [rel, 'capped'].join(SEP);
    48	    try {
    49	      const content = fs.readFileSync(cwd + '/' + rel, 'utf8');
    50	      return [rel, String(Buffer.byteLength(content)), sha256(content)].join(SEP);
    51	    } catch {
    52	      // Listed but unreadable (deleted mid-flight): still digest its presence.
    53	      return [rel, 'absent'].join(SEP);
    54	    }
    55	  });
    56	
    57	  return {
    58	    branch: branch.stdout.trim(),
    59	    headSha: head.stdout.trim(),
    60	    dirty: dirtySummary.length > 0,
    61	    dirtySummary,
    62	    contentDigest: sha256([staged.stdout, unstaged.stdout, ...untrackedEntries].join(SEP)),
    63	  };
    64	}

   127	  if (a[0] !== TOKEN_PREFIX || b[0] !== TOKEN_PREFIX || a.length !== b.length) return [];
   128	  return TOKEN_FIELDS.filter((_, i) => a[i + 1] !== b[i + 1]).map(([, name]) => name);

   167	  if (bundle === null) throw new Error(`no handoff bundle under ${root}/.handoff — nothing to receive`);

   204	        );
   205	      } else {
   206	        avoid = [deadOrigin];
   207	      }
   208	    }
   209	    assignments = resolveRoles({ config, to: opts.platform, avoid, nativeOnly: false, probes: opts.probes ?? null }).assignments;
   210	  } else {
   211	    warnings.push(`role matrix unavailable (${errors.map((e) => e.msg).join('; ')}) — no role table in this prompt`);
   212	  }
   213	
   214	  const prompt = renderResumePrompt({ bundle, assignments, warnings, origin: opts.origin, reason: opts.reason });
   215	  return { token: deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io), prompt, assignments, warnings };
   216	}

   218	/**
   219	 * Phase 2: one atomic transition. Re-derives every bound input from current
   220	 * disk state + opts and rejects ANY drift (throws, zero mutation). On match:
   221	 * writes the received seal, archives it via a 'receive' rotation, then opens a
   222	 * fresh writable generation owned by the receiving platform/session.
   223	 * @param {string} root @param {string} token @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
   224	 * @returns {{adopted: boolean, generation: number, archivedTo: string | null, alreadyCommitted?: boolean}}
   225	 */
   226	export function commit(root, token, opts, io) {
   227	  // ONE operation-scoped lock across revalidation and every mutation (gate-2
   228	  // fix: reviewers a#1/b#11): two competing receivers serialize here, and the
   229	  // loser's re-derivation sees the winner's generation/status/receive_log.
   230	  return withLock(root, io, (fence) => commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence));
   231	}
   232	
   233	/**
   234	 * @param {string} root @param {string} token @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io @param {string} fence
   235	 * @returns {{adopted: boolean, generation: number, archivedTo: string | null, alreadyCommitted?: boolean}}
   236	 */
   237	function commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence) {
   238	  const { bundle } = loadBundle(root, io);
   239	  if (bundle === null) throw new Error(`no handoff bundle under ${root}/.handoff — nothing to receive; run receive --prepare first`);
   240	  opts = effectiveIntake(bundle, opts);
   241	
   242	  const expected = deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io);
   243	  if (expected !== token) {
   244	    // Idempotency first (audit finding: duplicate-receive corruption): if THIS
   245	    // exact receipt already landed — its digest is recorded on a receive_log
   246	    // entry — the retry is a lost-output re-send, not drift. Report success
   247	    // with zero mutation instead of sending the model into a re-prepare +
   248	    // re-commit loop that executes a second full receive.
   249	    const receipt = dedupeKey(token).slice(0, 16);
   250	    const landed = Array.isArray(bundle.handoff?.receive_log) && bundle.handoff.receive_log.some((/** @type {any} */ e) => e?.receipt === receipt);
   251	    if (landed) {
   252	      return { adopted: false, alreadyCommitted: true, generation: bundle.generation, archivedTo: null };
   253	    }
   254	    const drifted = driftedInputs(token, expected);
   255	    const detail = drifted.length > 0 ? `drifted input(s): ${drifted.join(', ')}` : 'a bound input drifted since prepare';
   256	    throw new Error(
   257	      `receipt token is stale — ${detail}. Re-prepare and retry, passing the SAME intake flags (--origin/--reason/--reason-class) to both prepare and --commit`,
   258	    );
   259	  }
   260	
   261	  const degraded = bundle.handoff.status !== 'sealed';
   262	  const receiveEntry = {
   263	    origin: opts.origin,
   264	    reason: opts.reason,
   265	    at: io.now(),
   266	    // The receipt digest keys the idempotent-retry detection above.
   267	    receipt: dedupeKey(token).slice(0, 16),
   268	    ...(degraded ? { degradedSeal: true } : {}),
   269	  };
   270	
   271	  // The degraded seal must NOT persist a LOW-confidence classification (iter-3
   272	  // F10): a sealed reasonClass is trusted as high-confidence by the next
   273	  // prepare, so laundering a low-confidence heuristic here would silently
   274	  // auto-avoid the origin one hop later. Explicit intake is high-confidence and
   275	  // seals; a live classification seals ONLY at medium+ confidence, else null
   276	  // (the next receive re-classifies the reason text at its true confidence).
   277	  let sealedReasonClass = null;
   278	  if (degraded) {
   279	    if (typeof opts.reasonClass === 'string') {
   280	      sealedReasonClass = opts.reasonClass;
   281	    } else {
   282	      const v = classifyReason(opts.reason, opts.origin, io);
   283	      sealedReasonClass = v.confidence === 'low' ? null : v.class;
   284	    }
   285	  }
   286	
   287	  const receivedSeal = {
   288	    ...bundle,
   289	    updatedAt: io.now(),
   290	    handoff: {
   291	      ...bundle.handoff,
   292	      status: 'received',
   293	      ...(degraded
   294	        ? {
   295	            reason: opts.reason,
   296	            reasonClass: sealedReasonClass,
   297	            finalizedAt: io.now(),
   298	          }
   299	        : {}),
   300	      receive_log: [...bundle.handoff.receive_log, receiveEntry],
   301	    },
   302	  };
   303	
   304	  // Freeze order: the received seal is written first so the 'receive' rotation
   305	  // archives exactly that state (never the pre-commit bundle). All three
   306	  // mutations run under the SAME lock acquisition, fence-checked per write.
   307	  writeSnapshotIn(root, receivedSeal, io, fence);
   308	  const archivedTo = rotateJournalIn(root, 'receive', io, fence);
   309	
   310	  const { config } = loadConfig(root, io);
   311	  const next = {
   312	    ...receivedSeal,
   313	    generation: bundle.generation + 1,
   314	    origin: {
   315	      platform: opts.platform,
   316	      model: config?.defaults?.[opts.platform] ?? 'unknown',
   317	      sessionHint: opts.sessionHint,
   318	      unstable: opts.sessionUnstable === true,
   319	    },
   320	    // The fresh writable generation has NO switch reason yet (iter-4 I3): the
   321	    // sealed reason/reasonClass/finalizedAt/toPlatformHint describe the PRIOR
   322	    // handoff, not this one. Carrying them forward made the next prepare trust a
   323	    // stale class as a high-confidence seal (silently auto-avoiding the healthy
   324	    // adopted origin) and poisoned both the 12 h staleness reference and the
   325	    // sessionStart limit-hit signal. Keep only receive_log (the audit chain).
   326	    handoff: { ...receivedSeal.handoff, status: 'open', reason: null, reasonClass: null, finalizedAt: null, toPlatformHint: null },
   327	  };
   328	  writeSnapshotIn(root, next, io, fence);
   329	
   330	  return { adopted: true, generation: next.generation, archivedTo };
   331	}

    35	 */
    36	export async function cmdFinalize(args, io) {
    37	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(args, { reason: 'string', 'reason-class': 'string', to: 'string' });
    38	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'finalize', parsed.error);
    39	  const flags = parsed.flags;
    40	  const reason = typeof flags.reason === 'string' ? flags.reason : null;
    41	  if (!reason) return usageError(io, flags, 'finalize', '--reason "<why you are switching>" is required');
    42	  const toErr = platformError(flags.to);
    43	  if (toErr) return usageError(io, flags, 'finalize', `--to: ${toErr}`);
    44	  const REASON_CLASSES = ['usage-limit', 'auth', 'throttle', 'other-error'];
    45	  if (flags['reason-class'] !== undefined && !REASON_CLASSES.includes(/** @type {string} */ (flags['reason-class']))) {
    46	    return usageError(io, flags, 'finalize', `--reason-class must be one of ${REASON_CLASSES.join('|')}`);
    47	  }
    48	
    49	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
    50	  const paths = bundlePaths(root);
    51	  const { bundle, warnings } = loadBundle(root, io);
    52	  for (const w of warnings) io.stderr.write(`baton finalize: ${w}\n`);
    53	  if (bundle === null) {
    54	    const error = { code: 'no-bundle', msg: `no handoff bundle at ${paths.snapshot}; nothing to finalize` };
    55	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error });
    56	    else io.stderr.write(`baton finalize: ${error.msg}\n`);
    57	    return 1;
    58	  }
    59	
    60	  // Capture git BEFORE the lock — it is async and must not straddle the lock.
    61	  const git = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
    62	  if (git === null) io.stderr.write('baton finalize: git state unavailable — sealing with git marked unavailable (not the stale prior snapshot)\n');
    63	
    64	  // ONE atomic locked span (iter-5 A2): the seal, snapshot write, and journal
    65	  // rotation run under a SINGLE lock acquisition + fence, and the bundle is
    66	  // RELOADED inside the lock. The old code loaded before the async git await
    67	  // then sealed + wrote + rotated through separate locks, so a decision appended
    68	  // during the await was sealed from a stale bundle and survived only in the
    69	  // rotated journal. Reloading inside the lock includes it in the seal.
    70	  const sealed = withLock(root, io, (token) => {
    71	    const current = loadBundle(root, io).bundle;
    72	    if (current === null) return null; // deleted concurrently between the checks
    73	    const reasonClass =
    74	      typeof flags['reason-class'] === 'string' ? flags['reason-class'] : inferReasonClass(reason, current.origin.platform, io);
    75	    const s = {
    76	      ...current,
    77	      // NEVER seal the stale prior git snapshot (iter-4 I2 sibling): a receive
    78	      // audits the seal's git against live state, so stale HEAD/dirty would emit
    79	      // false "HEAD moved"/"dirty mismatch" warnings. On refresh failure seal an
    80	      // explicit unavailable (null) git; receive re-derives it live regardless.
    81	      git,
    82	      updatedAt: io.now(),
    83	      handoff: {
    84	        ...current.handoff,
    85	        status: 'sealed',
    86	        reason,
    87	        reasonClass,
    88	        toPlatformHint: typeof flags.to === 'string' ? flags.to : null,
    89	        finalizedAt: io.now(),
    90	      },
    91	    };
    92	    writeSnapshotIn(root, s, io, token);
    93	    rotateJournalIn(root, 'finalize', io, token);
    94	    return s;
    95	  });
    96	
    97	  if (sealed === null) {
    98	    const error = { code: 'no-bundle', msg: `handoff bundle vanished during finalize at ${paths.snapshot}` };
    99	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error });
   100	    else io.stderr.write(`baton finalize: ${error.msg}\n`);
   101	    return 1;
   102	  }
   103	
   104	  // Inference only matches verbatim harness banners; a natural paraphrase
   105	  // seals reasonClass:null — and receive's role remap only auto-avoids the dead
   106	  // platform on 'usage-limit'. Surface the gap instead of silently defeating
   107	  // the failover heuristics (audit finding).
   108	  if (sealed.handoff.reasonClass === null && flags['reason-class'] === undefined) {
   109	    io.stderr.write(
   110	      'baton finalize: no reason class inferred from the reason text — if this switch was forced, re-run with --reason-class <usage-limit|throttle|auth|other-error> so receive keeps roles off the exhausted platform\n',
   111	    );
   112	  }
   113	
   114	  if (flags.json) {
   115	    emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: { bundlePath: paths.snapshot, handoffMdPath: paths.handoffMd } });
   116	  } else {
   117	    const rc = sealed.handoff.reasonClass;
   118	    io.stdout.write(`sealed — reason: ${reason}${rc ? ` (${rc})` : ''}${sealed.handoff.toPlatformHint ? ` — next: ${sealed.handoff.toPlatformHint}` : ''}\n`);
   119	  }
   120	  return 0;
   121	}

    23	  // warns; this is the last-line guard for any direct caller.
    24	  if (event === null || typeof event !== 'object' || Array.isArray(event)) return bundle;
    25	  if (bundle.dedupeRing.includes(event.dedupeKey)) return bundle;
    26	
    27	  const out = structuredClone(bundle);
    28	  const { seq, ts, type, payload = {} } = structuredClone(event);
    29	
    30	  switch (type) {
    31	    case 'decision': {
    32	      /** @type {{seq: number, ts: string, summary: any, detail?: any}} */
    33	      const entry = { seq, ts, summary: payload.summary };
    34	      if (payload.detail !== undefined) entry.detail = payload.detail;
    35	      out.decisions.push(entry);
    36	      break;
    37	    }
    38	    case 'note':
    39	      out.decisions.push({ seq, ts, summary: payload.text });
    40	      // A structured StopFailure rate_limit note marks the open bundle
    41	      // limit-hit (gate-2 fix 3): the unsealed limit death must be visible to
    42	      // the next SessionStart on any platform, not buried in the decision log.
    43	      if (payload.structured?.kind === 'stop-failure' && payload.errorType === 'rate_limit' && out.handoff.status === 'open') {
    44	        out.handoff = { ...out.handoff, reason: out.handoff.reason ?? payload.text ?? null, reasonClass: 'usage-limit' };
    45	      }
    46	      break;
    47	    case 'plan.set':
    48	      if (Array.isArray(payload.steps) && payload.steps.every((/** @type {any} */ s) => s !== null && typeof s === 'object')) {
    49	        out.plan.steps = payload.steps;
    50	      } else {
    51	        out.decisions.push({ seq, ts, summary: refusalNote('plan.set', payload?.steps) });
    52	      }
    53	      break;
    54	    case 'plan.step': {
    55	      if (payload === null || typeof payload !== 'object' || typeof payload.id !== 'string') {
    56	        out.decisions.push({ seq, ts, summary: refusalNote('plan.step', payload) });
    57	        break;
    58	      }
    59	      const existing = out.plan.steps.find((/** @type {any} */ s) => s.id === payload.id);
    60	      if (existing) Object.assign(existing, payload);
    61	      else out.plan.steps.push(payload);
    62	      break;
    63	    }
    64	    case 'file.touch': {
    65	      const safePath = jailRelPath(payload?.path);
    66	      if (safePath === null) {
    67	        out.decisions.push({ seq, ts, summary: refusalNote('file.touch', payload?.path) });
    68	        break;
    69	      }
    70	      const entry = { path: safePath, op: typeof payload.op === 'string' ? payload.op : 'touch', lastTs: ts };
    71	      const i = out.files.touched.findIndex((/** @type {any} */ f) => f.path === safePath);
    72	      if (i === -1) out.files.touched.push(entry);
    73	      else out.files.touched[i] = entry;
    74	      break;
    75	    }
    76	    case 'roles.remap': {
    77	      // The assignments object AND every value must be non-null objects (iter-3
    78	      // F3): a well-formed {planner: null} used to be stored verbatim and then
    79	      // crashed renderHandoffMd. Untrusted journal input degrades to a note.
    80	      const a = payload?.assignments;
    81	      const wellFormed =
    82	        a !== null &&
    83	        typeof a === 'object' &&
    84	        !Array.isArray(a) &&
    85	        Object.values(a).every((/** @type {any} */ v) => v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v));
    86	      if (wellFormed) {
    87	        out.roles.assignments = a;
    88	      } else {
    89	        out.decisions.push({ seq, ts, summary: refusalNote('roles.remap', a) });
    90	      }
    91	      break;
    92	    }
    93	    case 'task.update': {
    94	      /** @type {Record<string, any>} */
    95	      const patch = {};
    96	      if (typeof payload?.goal === 'string') patch.goal = payload.goal;
    97	      if (Array.isArray(payload?.constraints) && payload.constraints.every((/** @type {any} */ c) => typeof c === 'string')) {
    98	        patch.constraints = payload.constraints;
    99	      }
   100	      if (Array.isArray(payload?.acceptance)) patch.acceptance = payload.acceptance;
   101	      if (Object.keys(patch).length === 0) {
   102	        out.decisions.push({ seq, ts, summary: refusalNote('task.update', payload) });
   103	        break;
   104	      }
   105	      out.task = { ...out.task, ...patch };
   106	      break;
   107	    }
   108	    case 'git.update':
   109	      if (payload === null || typeof payload === 'object') out.git = payload;
   110	      else out.decisions.push({ seq, ts, summary: refusalNote('git.update', payload) });
   111	      break;
   112	    case 'bundle.seed':
   113	      // Self-applying identity (gate-2 iter-2 B6): the auto-seed emits this as
   114	      // the journal's first event so a journal-only rebuild (snapshot + .bak
   115	      // both gone) restores the bundle's identity/origin/task instead of the
   116	      // "unknown" placeholder resolveBase seeds. Replayed first (lowest seq),
   117	      // so later events layer on top; on normal replay its seq is below the
   118	      // snapshot's journalSeq and it is skipped.
   119	      if (payload && typeof payload === 'object') {
   120	        if (typeof payload.bundleId === 'string') out.bundleId = payload.bundleId;
   121	        if (typeof payload.generation === 'number') out.generation = payload.generation;
   122	        if (typeof payload.createdAt === 'string') out.createdAt = payload.createdAt;
   123	        // Restore identity ONLY (platform/model) — never sessionHint/unstable.
   124	        // Session ownership is adopted AFTER the seed (a snapshot-only mutation),
   125	        // so replaying the seed must not clobber a later-adopted hint back to
   126	        // its seed-time null (gate-2 iter-2: caught by the adoption test).
   127	        if (payload.origin && typeof payload.origin === 'object') {
   128	          if (typeof payload.origin.platform === 'string') out.origin.platform = payload.origin.platform;
   129	          if (typeof payload.origin.model === 'string') out.origin.model = payload.origin.model;
   130	        }
   131	        if (payload.task && typeof payload.task === 'object' && typeof payload.task.goal === 'string') {
   132	          out.task.goal = payload.task.goal;
   133	        }
   134	      }
   135	      break;
   136	    case 'transcript.set':
   137	      // Opt-in transcript tail (plan §Transcript policy): stored under the
   138	      // literal property name `transcript` so purge-transcript strips it from
   139	      // every retained copy. Render never includes it.
   140	      if (payload?.transcript !== null && typeof payload?.transcript === 'object' && typeof payload.transcript.tail === 'string') {
   141	        out.transcript = {
   142	          capturedAt: typeof payload.transcript.capturedAt === 'string' ? payload.transcript.capturedAt : ts,
   143	          tail: payload.transcript.tail,
   144	        };
   145	      } else {
   146	        out.decisions.push({ seq, ts, summary: refusalNote('transcript.set', 'malformed payload') });
   147	      }
   148	      break;
   149	    default:
   150	      out.decisions.push({ seq, ts, summary: `[unhandled event type '${type}' recorded as note]` });
   151	      break;
   152	  }
   153	
   154	  out.updatedAt = ts;
   155	  // Harden against foreign/keyless entries (gate-2 fix): a missing seq must
   156	  // never poison journalSeq to NaN, and an absent dedupeKey must never enter
   157	  // the ring (undefined in the ring dedupes every later keyless event).
   158	  if (typeof seq === 'number' && Number.isFinite(seq)) out.journalSeq = Math.max(out.journalSeq, seq);
   159	  if (typeof event.dedupeKey === 'string' && event.dedupeKey.length > 0) {
   160	    out.dedupeRing.push(event.dedupeKey);
   161	    if (out.dedupeRing.length > RING_CAP) out.dedupeRing.splice(0, out.dedupeRing.length - RING_CAP);
   162	  }
   163	
   164	  return out;
   165	}

     1	/**
     2	 * Pure, explainable role resolution over the committed matrix. Every decision
     3	 * is auditable: chosen entries carry their chainIndex; passed-over entries land
     4	 * in skipped[] with a why. avoid[] population is the caller's job.
     5	 * @param {{config: any, to: string, avoid?: string[], avoidEntries?: Array<{platform: string, model: string}>, nativeOnly?: boolean, probes?: Record<string, {capability: string, outcome: string}> | null}} input
     6	 * @returns {{assignments: Record<string, any>, notes: string[]}}
     7	 */
     8	export function resolveRoles({ config, to, avoid = [], avoidEntries = [], nativeOnly = false, probes = null }) {
     9	  /** @type {string[]} */
    10	  const notes = [];
    11	
    12	  /**
    13	   * The eligibility verdict for a platform, or null when eligible.
    14	   * @param {string} platform @returns {string | null}
    15	   */
    16	  function skipReason(platform) {
    17	    if (avoid.includes(platform)) return 'avoided';
    18	    if (!(platform in (config.platforms ?? {}))) return 'unknown-platform';
    19	    if (config.platforms[platform]?.enabled === false) return 'disabled';
    20	    if (probes && probes[platform]) {
    21	      const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    22	      if (outcome === 'rate-limited') return 'rate-limited';
    23	      if (capability === 'not-installed') return 'not-installed';
    24	      // 'installed' means installation was PROVEN but the probe was capped there
    25	      // (capOnSuccess) — authentication is UNVERIFIED, not verified-failed. Only
    26	      // a probe that ran and did NOT succeed (outcome !== 'ok') is a verified
    27	      // auth/reachability failure worth skipping; a capped success stays
    28	      // selectable and is flagged degraded below (iter-3 F1, plan §Role matrix).
    29	      if (capability === 'installed' && outcome !== 'ok') return 'unauthenticated';
    30	    }
    31	    return null;
    32	  }
    33	
    34	  // A selection is degraded when its availability is UNVERIFIED (gate-2 iter-2
    35	  // M3, iter-3 F1): with no probe cache at all, resolution is offline and EVERY
    36	  // selection is degraded (plan: "Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged
    37	  // degraded"); with a partial cache, platforms the cache is missing are; and a
    38	  // platform probed only to 'installed' (auth unverified, e.g. a --version
    39	  // success) is degraded even though it stays selectable.
    40	  /** @param {string} platform */
    41	  const probeUnverified = (platform) => {
    42	    if (probes == null || !probes[platform]) return true;
    43	    const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    44	    // Degraded when ANY required dimension is unverified: a capped 'installed'
    45	    // (auth never confirmed) OR a non-ok outcome (iter-4 I6) — a selectable
    46	    // platform whose last probe ERRORED or TIMED OUT is presented as
    47	    // reachability-verified otherwise, which is exactly the silent-degradation
    48	    // the plan's degraded flag exists to surface. (rate-limited is skipped, not
    49	    // selected, so it never reaches here.)
    50	    return capability === 'installed' || outcome !== 'ok';
    51	  };
    52	
    53	  // Entry-level avoidance (plan §Model-level failover): a specific
    54	  // {platform, model} tuple is dead (e.g. account-tier rejected) while its
    55	  // platform stays usable. Matching is on model IDENTITY — an @effort suffix
    56	  // on either side is ignored — and requires BOTH dimensions, so the same
    57	  // model name on another platform is never caught.
    58	  /** @param {any} m */
    59	  const baseModel = (m) => (typeof m === 'string' ? m.split('@')[0] : m);
    60	  /** @param {string} platform @param {string} model */
    61	  const entryAvoided = (platform, model) =>
    62	    avoidEntries.some((a) => a?.platform === platform && baseModel(a?.model) === baseModel(model));
    63	
    64	  /** @type {Record<string, any>} */
    65	  const assignments = {};
    66	  for (const [role, chain] of Object.entries(config.roles)) {
    67	    /** @type {any[]} */
    68	    const skipped = [];
    69	    /** @type {any} */
    70	    let assignment = null;
    71	
    72	    for (let i = 0; i < chain.length; i += 1) {
    73	      const entry = chain[i];
    74	      if (nativeOnly && entry.platform !== to) {
    75	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'non-native' });
    76	        continue;
    77	      }
    78	      const why = skipReason(entry.platform);
    79	      if (why) {
    80	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why });
    81	        continue;
    82	      }
    83	      // After skipReason so a dual match keeps the platform-level label.
    84	      if (entryAvoided(entry.platform, entry.model)) {
    85	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'avoided-entry' });
    86	        continue;
    87	      }
    88	      assignment = {
    89	        platform: entry.platform,
    90	        model: entry.model,
    91	        effort: entry.effort ?? null,
    92	        mode: entry.platform === to ? 'native' : 'delegated',
    93	        chainIndex: i,
    94	        skipped,
    95	      };
    96	      if (probeUnverified(entry.platform)) assignment.degraded = true;
    97	      break;
    98	    }
    99	
   100	    if (!assignment && nativeOnly) {
   101	      // Forced-default is only valid when the destination itself is eligible.
   102	      const whyTo = skipReason(to);
   103	      const model = config.defaults?.[to];
   104	      if (!whyTo && typeof model === 'string') {
   105	        assignment = { platform: to, model, effort: null, mode: 'forced-default', chainIndex: null, skipped };
   106	        if (probeUnverified(to)) assignment.degraded = true;
   107	      }
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    if (!assignment) {
   111	      assignment = { platform: null, model: null, effort: null, mode: 'unavailable', chainIndex: null, skipped };
   112	    }
   113	    assignments[role] = assignment;
   114	  }
   115	
   116	  return { assignments, notes };
   117	}

    10	 * any nested group inside a `(…)+`/`(…)*`/`(…){` makes backtracking
    11	 * super-linear in the worst case — conservatively rejected (gate-2 fix 6:
    12	 * the old lint accepted `(a|aa)+$` and the `(a|a)*x` live repro).

    15	function riskyGroupBody(body) {
    16	  // Strip a non-capture/lookaround/named marker so `(?:abc)+` reads as `abc`.
    17	  const b = body.replace(/^\?(?:<=|<!|:|=|!|<[^>]*>)/, '');

    61	    }
    62	    if (c === '(') {
    63	      opens.push(i);
    64	      continue;
    65	    }
    66	    if (c === ')') {
    67	      const start = opens.pop();
    68	      if (start === undefined) continue; // unbalanced — new RegExp() reports it
    69	      const next = pattern[i + 1];
    70	      if (next === '+' || next === '*' || next === '{') {
    71	        const body = pattern.slice(start + 1, i);
    72	        if (riskyGroupBody(body)) {
    73	          return `quantified group "(${body})" contains alternation, another quantifier, or a nested group`;
    74	        }
    75	      }
    76	    }
    77	  }
    78	  return null;
    79	}
    80	
    81	/**
    82	 * Approximate character-set overlap between two simple-atom alphabets.
    83	 * Descriptors: {all:true} (dot / broad negated shorthand) | {sh:'d'|'w'|'s'} |
    84	 * {lit:Set<string>}. Returns true unless the two sets are PROVABLY disjoint —
    85	 * conservative for untrusted overlays (iter-4 I4).
    86	 * @param {any} a @param {any} b
    87	 */
    88	function alphasOverlap(a, b) {
    89	  if (!a || !b) return false;
    90	  if (a.all || b.all) return true;
    91	  if (a.sh && b.sh) {
    92	    if (a.sh === b.sh) return true;
    93	    // \s is disjoint from \d and \w; \d ⊂ \w so they overlap.
    94	    return !(a.sh === 's' || b.sh === 's');
    95	  }
    96	  if (a.lit && b.lit) {
    97	    for (const c of a.lit) if (b.lit.has(c)) return true;
    98	    return false;
    99	  }
   100	  const sh = a.sh ? a.sh : b.sh;
   101	  const lit = a.lit ? a.lit : b.lit;
   102	  for (const c of lit) {
   103	    if (sh === 'd' && c >= '0' && c <= '9') return true;
   104	    if (sh === 'w' && /[A-Za-z0-9_]/.test(c)) return true;
   105	    if (sh === 's' && /\s/.test(c)) return true;
   106	  }
   107	  return false;
   108	}
   109	
   110	/**
   111	 * Structural scan for a run of ≥2 CONSECUTIVE atoms, each with an UNBOUNDED
   112	 * quantifier (`*`, `+`, `{n,}`), whose alphabets overlap — `.*.*…`, `\d*\d*…`,
   113	 * `\(*\(*…`, `\n*\n*…`, `[a-z]*[a-z]*…`. Such a chain partitions the same input
   114	 * combinatorially and backtracks super-linearly, yet is invisible to the
   115	 * quantified-GROUP scan; and because a finite probe alphabet cannot guarantee a
   116	 * non-matching tail for every atom (`.` accepts almost everything), rejecting
   117	 * the STRUCTURE at load is the reliable guard (iter-4 I4, reviewer-a #7 /
   118	 * reviewer-b #3). Groups reset the run (the group scan covers quantified groups;
   119	 * a group's overlap with a simple atom is not decided here). Returns a problem
   120	 * string or null.
   121	 * @param {string} pattern
   122	 * @returns {string | null}
   123	 */
   124	function scanChainedQuantifiedAtoms(pattern) {
   125	  const p = pattern;
   126	  /** @type {any} */
   127	  let prev = null; // alpha of the previous atom IF it carried an unbounded quantifier, else null
   128	
   129	  for (let i = 0; i < p.length; ) {
   130	    const c = p[i];
   131	    // Chain-breakers: alternation and anchors end any run.
   132	    if (c === '|' || c === '^' || c === '$') {
   133	      prev = null;
   134	      i += 1;
   135	      continue;
   136	    }
   137	    /** @type {any} */
   138	    let alpha = null;
   139	    let isGroup = false;
   140	    if (c === '\\') {
   141	      const n = p[i + 1];
   142	      // decode length of the escape token
   143	      let len = 2;
   144	      if (n === 'x') len = 4;
   145	      else if (n === 'u') len = p[i + 2] === '{' ? (p.indexOf('}', i) - i + 1) : 6;
   146	      if (n === 'd' || n === 'w' || n === 's') alpha = { sh: n };
   147	      else if (n === 'D' || n === 'W' || n === 'S' || n === 'b' || n === 'B') alpha = { all: true }; // broad/negated or anchor-ish → conservative
   148	      else alpha = { lit: new Set([decodeEscape(p.slice(i, i + len))]) }; // \(, \n, \t, \xNN, \uNNNN → the literal char
   149	      i += Math.max(2, len);
   150	    } else if (c === '[') {
   151	      const end = classEnd(p, i);
   152	      const body = p.slice(i + 1, end);
   153	      alpha = body.startsWith('^') ? { all: true } : classAlpha(body);
   154	      i = end + 1;
   155	    } else if (c === '(') {
   156	      // Skip the whole group (balance-aware); recurse into its body for chains.
   157	      const end = groupEnd(p, i);
   158	      const inner = scanChainedQuantifiedAtoms(p.slice(i + 1, end));
   159	      if (inner) return inner;
   160	      isGroup = true;
     1	const PRECEDENCE = ['usage-limit', 'auth', 'model-unavailable', 'throttle', 'other-error'];
     2	
     3	/** @type {Record<string, string>} */
     4	const STOP_FAILURE_MAP = {
     5	  rate_limit: 'usage-limit',
     6	  overloaded: 'throttle',
     7	  authentication_failed: 'auth',
     8	  oauth_org_not_allowed: 'auth',
     9	  billing_error: 'auth',
    10	};

    12	// eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
    13	const ANSI = /\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]/g;
    14	
    15	/** @param {any} matcher @param {string} text */
    16	function matches(matcher, text) {
    17	  switch (matcher.kind) {
    18	    case 'substring':
    19	      return text.includes(matcher.value);
    20	    case 'regex':
    21	      return new RegExp(matcher.pattern, matcher.flags || '').test(text);
    22	    case 'json-field': {
    23	      for (const line of text.split('\n')) {
    24	        let obj;
    25	        try {
    26	          obj = JSON.parse(line);
    27	        } catch {
    28	          continue;
    29	        }
    30	        const val = String(matcher.path)
    31	          .split('.')
    32	          .reduce((o, k) => (o == null ? undefined : o[k]), obj);
    33	        if (val === matcher.equals) return true;
    34	      }
    35	      return false;
    36	    }
    37	    default:
    38	      return false;
    39	  }
    40	}
    41	
    42	/**
    43	 * Classify harness output. Structured evidence first (text and exit code are
    44	 * ignored when a recognized structured signal is present); text signatures as
    45	 * the fallback tier; exit code only breaks the no-match tie — a generic nonzero
    46	 * exit is never usage-limit on its own.
    47	 * @param {{text?: string, exitCode?: number, platform: string, table: any, structured?: {kind: string, errorType: string} | null}} input
    48	 * @returns {{class: string, signatureId: string | null, confidence: string | null, resetHint: string | null, tried?: string[]}}
    49	 */
    50	export function classify({ text = '', exitCode = 0, platform, table, structured = null }) {
    51	  if (structured) {
    52	    if (structured.kind === 'stop-failure') {
    53	      const cls = STOP_FAILURE_MAP[structured.errorType] ?? 'other-error';
    54	      return { class: cls, signatureId: `structured:${structured.errorType}`, confidence: 'high', resetHint: null };
    55	    }
    56	    if (structured.kind === 'exec-json') {
    57	      const cls = structured.errorType === 'usage_limit' ? 'usage-limit' : 'other-error';
    58	      return { class: cls, signatureId: `structured:${structured.errorType}`, confidence: 'high', resetHint: null };
    59	    }
    60	    // Unrecognized structured kind: fall through to the text tier.
    61	  }
    62	
    63	  const stripped = text.replace(ANSI, '');
    64	  const candidates = table.signatures.filter((/** @type {any} */ s) => s.platform === platform);
    65	  /** @type {any} */
    66	  let best = null;
    67	  for (const s of candidates) {
    68	    if (!matches(s.matcher, stripped)) continue;
    69	    if (best === null || PRECEDENCE.indexOf(s.class) < PRECEDENCE.indexOf(best.class)) best = s;
    70	  }
    71	
    72	  if (best) {
    73	    let resetHint = null;
    74	    if (typeof best.resetHint === 'string') {
    75	      const m = stripped.match(new RegExp(best.resetHint));
    76	      if (m) resetHint = m[1] ?? m[0];
    77	    }
    78	    return { class: best.class, signatureId: best.id, confidence: best.confidence, resetHint };
    79	  }
    80	
    81	  return {
    82	    class: exitCode !== 0 ? 'other-error' : 'ok',
    83	    signatureId: null,
    84	    confidence: null,
    85	    resetHint: null,
    86	  };
    87	}

   260	/** Approximate alphabet of a (non-negated) class body: literals + range endpoints + shorthands. @param {string} body */
   261	function classAlpha(body) {
   262	  if (/\\[dwsDWS]/.test(body) || /\\[DWS]/.test(body)) return { all: true }; // shorthand inside a class → treat broadly
   263	  /** @type {Set<string>} */
   264	  const lit = new Set();
   265	  for (let i = 0; i < body.length; i++) {
   266	    if (body[i] === '\\') {
   267	      lit.add(decodeEscape(body.slice(i, i + 2)));
   268	      i += 1;
   269	      continue;
   270	    }
   271	    // range a-z: add endpoints (a run of an endpoint char backtracks the same)
   272	    if (body[i + 1] === '-' && body[i + 2] !== undefined) {
   273	      lit.add(body[i]);
   274	      lit.add(body[i + 2]);
   275	      i += 2;
   276	      continue;
   277	    }
   278	    lit.add(body[i]);
   279	  }
   280	  return { lit };
   281	}

   285	/**
   286	 * Validate a regex flags string (gate-2 iter-2 B3): every char must be an
   287	 * allowed JS flag with no duplicates, so a flags value that compiles nowhere
   288	 * (`z`, `ii`) is rejected at LOAD, not left to throw later inside classify().
   289	 * @param {string} id @param {string} flags
   290	 */
   291	function lintFlags(id, flags) {
   292	  if (typeof flags !== 'string') throw new Error(`signature ${id}: regex flags must be a string`);
   293	  const seen = new Set();
   294	  for (const c of flags) {
   295	    if (!ALLOWED_FLAGS.includes(c)) throw new Error(`signature ${id}: unsupported regex flag "${c}" (allowed: ${ALLOWED_FLAGS})`);
   296	    if (seen.has(c)) throw new Error(`signature ${id}: duplicate regex flag "${c}"`);
   297	    seen.add(c);
   298	  }
   299	}

   301	/**
   302	 * Lint one regex pattern together with its flags. With the load-time worker
   303	 * probe on overlay tables (see probe.mjs), the runtime time-guard is by
   304	 * construction: patterns that could backtrack catastrophically never reach
   305	 * classify(), which stays synchronous with no timers.
   306	 * @param {string} id @param {string} pattern @param {string} [flags]
   307	 */
   308	function lintRegex(id, pattern, flags = '') {
   309	  if (typeof pattern !== 'string' || pattern.length > REGEX_MAX_LEN) {
   310	    throw new Error(`signature ${id}: regex pattern exceeds the ${REGEX_MAX_LEN}-char length cap (or is not a string)`);
   311	  }
   312	  if (/\\[1-9]/.test(pattern)) {
   313	    throw new Error(`signature ${id}: regex backreferences are not allowed`);
   314	  }
   315	  lintFlags(id, flags);
   316	  const problem = scanQuantifiedGroups(pattern) || scanChainedQuantifiedAtoms(pattern);
   317	  if (problem) {

   319	  }

   321	    // eslint-disable-next-line no-new

   323	  } catch (err) {
   324	    throw new Error(`signature ${id}: invalid regex pattern/flags (${/** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? 'syntax error'})`);
   325	  }
   326	}

docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

The portability standards to build on already exist: AGENTS.md (Linux Foundation/AAIF-governed; native in Codex + Cursor; bridged into Claude Code via an `@AGENTS.md` import in CLAUDE.md) and the Agent Skills standard (SKILL.md; native in Claude Code + Codex).

reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-01/raw-output.txt:320:    30	- **Codex plugin (installed, v1.0.4) is the implementation pattern**: single Node entrypoint invoked as `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<x>.mjs" <subcmd>`; hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` (SessionStart/SessionEnd/Stop) read event JSON on stdin and can emit `{"decision":"block","reason":…}`; commands/agents/skills as markdown with frontmatter; per-workspace state dir; structured-output JSON schemas for reviews. reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-01/raw-output.txt:348:    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-12-gate-2-final/reviewer-a/iteration-05/raw-output.txt:182:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-03/raw-output.txt:9259:  1469	   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:1441:   320	    30	- **Codex plugin (installed, v1.0.4) is the implementation pattern**: single Node entrypoint invoked as `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<x>.mjs" <subcmd>`; hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` (SessionStart/SessionEnd/Stop) read event JSON on stdin and can emit `{"decision":"block","reason":…}`; commands/agents/skills as markdown with frontmatter; per-workspace state dir; structured-output JSON schemas for reviews. reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:1469:   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:1677:   556	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-04/raw-output.txt:1225:   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-04/raw-output.txt:9676:  1469	   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.
