reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-04/raw-output.txt:19077:   808	   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

   126	  structured output format and the parser reads the result field; codex
   127	  children are parsed strictly AFTER the last `tokens used` marker. The
   128	  prompt region (which quotes `VERDICT:` in its instructions) is never
   129	  scanned. Multiple tails in the final region → the LAST one wins.
   130	- An unparseable, absent, or truncated verdict is BLOCKED-with-escalation,
   131	  never APPROVED; a child that exits after making edits but before a verdict
   132	  parks the subtask with its worktree preserved for inspection.

   134	  rule) → the loop retries once, then parks; it NEVER triggers limit failover

   137	  transcript, timeout kill/reap, zombie grandchild, non-limit nonzero exit.
   138	
   139	### Supervisor lifetime and recovery (Gate-1 iteration 2, finding 5)
   140	
   141	"Survives the operator's session ending" is a defined mechanism, not a hope:
   142	
   143	- `baton loop run` is FOREGROUND by default. `--detach` re-launches the
   144	  supervisor in its own session (`setsid`), output to
   145	  `.handoff/loop/supervisor.log`, and returns.
   146	- A run lock `.handoff/loop/supervisor.lock` carries {pid, process
   147	  start-time, host, runId} — the same provably-dead machinery as the
   148	  Layer-1 bundle lock. A second `loop run` against a LIVE supervisor is
   149	  refused; against a provably-dead one it recovers.
   150	- The state machine is journal-replayable: recovery replays
   151	  `journal.ndjson`, marks any in-flight child of the dead supervisor as
   152	  interrupted (its process group is gone or killed on adoption), and either
   153	  continues from the last completed step or parks with an escalation note —
   154	  never re-runs a completed gate iteration.
   155	- Acceptance adds a supervisor-death test: kill the supervisor (and its
   156	  launching session) mid-subtask → a fresh `loop run` recovers via the
   157	  journal and continues or parks; no orphaned children survive (process
   158	  groups reaped on adoption).
   159	
   160	- **Smoke gate (staleness-proof — Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 8; TDD order —
   161	  iteration 2, finding 2)**: after gate-1, the smoke slice is built as a TDD
   162	  mini-cycle (test-author writes the failing smoke assertion → test-verifier
   163	  approves it → implementer writes only enough to pass it — the repo TDD
   164	  contract applies to the slice, not just to subtasks); the supervisor then
   165	  runs `smoke.cmd`, records output, and STOPS, writing
   166	  `.handoff/loop/SMOKE-REVIEW.md` plus `smoke-approval.json` containing an
   167	  approval token = digest over {loop-state digest, smoke.cmd, output digest,
   168	  HEAD, content-sensitive git digest (existing snapshot machinery), child
   169	  assignment}. Resuming requires `baton loop run --approve-smoke <token>`;
   170	  the supervisor recomputes the digest first and REFUSES a drifted token
   171	  (anything changed since the human looked) — it parks for a fresh smoke run
   172	  instead. No full-run budget is spent before a valid approval.
   173	- **Limit failover (the baton integration — Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 3)**:
   174	  an exact transaction, not a loose chain. On child death: (1) reap the
   175	  process group and freeze the transcript; (2) classify via `baton detect`;
   176	  non-limit → the retry/park path above. On a limit classification:
   177	  (3) checkpoint the loop position INTO THE BUNDLE (supervisor
   178	  `checkpoint --session loop-<runId>`) so the seal carries it and the receipt
   179	  token binds it; (4) seal via `finalize --reason-class usage-limit --root
   180	  <mainRoot>` (an already-dead/unsealed bundle takes the degraded-open path
   181	  receive already supports); (5) refresh probes; (6) `receive --prepare` then
   182	  `--commit` back-to-back with IDENTICAL intake flags, the supervisor session
   183	  hint, and the same explicit root, with NO intervening writes; (7) resolver
   184	  output (with the dead entry avoided) picks the relaunch platform+model;
   185	  (8) relaunch the child with the resume prompt. A stale-token rejection
   186	  triggers ONE automatic re-prepare/commit retry; a second failure parks.
   187	  Between prepare and commit the failover holds the loop transaction lock and
   188	  writes NOTHING — `.handoff/loop/` writes are not token-bound inputs, so
   189	  this is enforced by construction and ASSERTED in tests (fs spy: zero
   190	  `.handoff/loop/` writes inside the window), not assumed. Drift-rejection
   191	  tests inject the inputs the token actually binds: git change and probe
   192	  refresh between prepare and commit → stale-token → one retry path. Plus:
   193	  open-bundle (unsealed) limit death; the full seal→receive→relaunch happy
   194	  path.
   195	- **Model-level failover (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 4)**: the resolver
   196	  gains entry-level avoidance — `avoidEntries: [{platform, model}]` alongside
   197	  the existing platform-level `avoid[]` — and the classifier gains a
   198	  `model-unavailable` signature class (distinct from usage-limit; seeded with
   199	  the verified account-tier rejection string). A model rejected at spawn adds
   200	  its {platform, model} entry to avoidEntries and re-resolves: other models
   201	  on the SAME platform remain selectable. Named test: first chain entry
   202	  rejected as model-unavailable → the next entry on the same platform is
   203	  selected, with no platform-wide avoidance.
   204	  All platforms/entries exhausted → the loop parks with a resume-at hint
   205	  instead of dying.

   379	export function loadSignatures({ builtinPath, overlayPath }, io) {
   380	  const base = readTable(io.fs, builtinPath);
   381	  if (!overlayPath) return base;
   382	
   383	  const overlay = readTable(io.fs, overlayPath, { probe: true });
   384	  const merged = [...base.signatures];
   385	  for (const s of overlay.signatures) {
   386	    const i = merged.findIndex((b) => b.id === s.id);
   387	    if (i === -1) merged.push(s);
   388	    else merged[i] = s;
   389	  }
   390	  return { ...base, updated: overlay.updated ?? base.updated, signatures: merged };
   391	}

   135	// A git execFile whose HEAD is chosen per rev-parse-HEAD call (the drift seam),
   136	// and which counts those calls so a test can pin the exact number of
   137	// prepare->commit windows. gitSnapshot reads clean status/diffs.
   138	function gitExec(headForCall) {
   139	  let headCalls = 0;
   140	  const fn = (/** @type {string} */ cmd, /** @type {string[]} */ args = []) => {
   141	    if (cmd !== 'git') return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('spawn ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }));
   142	    const key = args.join(' ');
   143	    if (key === 'rev-parse HEAD') {
   144	      headCalls += 1;
   145	      return Promise.resolve({ stdout: headForCall(headCalls) + '\n', stderr: '' });
   146	    }
   147	    const out = key === 'rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD' ? 'main' : '';
   148	    return Promise.resolve({ stdout: out + '\n', stderr: '' });
   149	  };
   150	  fn.headCalls = () => headCalls;
   151	  return fn;
   152	}

    81	  let configDigest = 'absent';
    82	  try {
    83	    configDigest = dedupeKey(io.fs.readFileSync(`${root}/baton.config.json`, 'utf8'));
    84	  } catch {

    93	    handoffStatus: bundle.handoff?.status ?? null,

   226	export function commit(root, token, opts, io) {
   227	  // ONE operation-scoped lock across revalidation and every mutation (gate-2
   228	  // fix: reviewers a#1/b#11): two competing receivers serialize here, and the
   229	  // loser's re-derivation sees the winner's generation/status/receive_log.
   230	  return withLock(root, io, (fence) => commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence));
   231	}
   232	
   233	/**
   234	 * @param {string} root @param {string} token @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io @param {string} fence
   235	 * @returns {{adopted: boolean, generation: number, archivedTo: string | null, alreadyCommitted?: boolean}}
   236	 */
   237	function commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence) {
   238	  const { bundle } = loadBundle(root, io);
   239	  if (bundle === null) throw new Error(`no handoff bundle under ${root}/.handoff — nothing to receive; run receive --prepare first`);
   240	  opts = effectiveIntake(bundle, opts);
   241	
   242	  const expected = deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io);
   243	  if (expected !== token) {
   244	    // Idempotency first (audit finding: duplicate-receive corruption): if THIS
   245	    // exact receipt already landed — its digest is recorded on a receive_log
   246	    // entry — the retry is a lost-output re-send, not drift. Report success
   247	    // with zero mutation instead of sending the model into a re-prepare +
   248	    // re-commit loop that executes a second full receive.

   250	    const landed = Array.isArray(bundle.handoff?.receive_log) && bundle.handoff.receive_log.some((/** @type {any} */ e) => e?.receipt === receipt);

   257	      `receipt token is stale — ${detail}. Re-prepare and retry, passing the SAME intake flags (--origin/--reason/--reason-class) to both prepare and --commit`,
   258	    );

     2	// { cwd, env, stdin, stdout, stderr, fs, execFile, now }. Backed by memfs.
     3	// stdout/stderr collect writes; io.stdoutText()/io.stderrText() flatten them.

     5	// execResults map keyed by the joined command string.
     6	//
     7	// Wave-B2 additions (bundle lock layer) — all optional, defaulted, and purely
     8	// additive so no prior consumer is affected:
     9	//   host / pid / startTime  — the process-identity facts the lock model writes

    12	//   processAlive(pid, startTime) — the "provably dead" oracle. Default: only
    13	//     THIS io's own {pid, startTime} is alive; every other descriptor reads as
    14	//     dead. Override per test to model a live foreign owner or a pid/start-time
    15	//     mismatch (reused pid).
    16	//   newFencingToken() — the injected per-acquisition token source. Deterministic
    17	//     monotonic counter ("tok-1", "tok-2", …), matching the injected-io
    18	//     discipline already used for now()/execFile so lock acquisition is
    19	//     reproducible in tests rather than drawing from Math.random.
    20	
    21	import { makeMemfs } from './memfs.mjs';
    22	
    23	export function makeIo({
    24	  files = {},
    25	  env = {},
    26	  stdin = '',
    27	  execResults = {},
    28	  now = '2026-07-11T00:00:00.000Z',
    29	  host = 'host-A',
    30	  pid = 4242,
    31	  startTime = 111000,
    32	  processAlive = null,
    33	  fencingSeed = 1,
    34	  execPath = process.execPath,
    35	} = {}) {
    36	  const { fs, files: filesSnapshot } = makeMemfs(files);
    37	  const outChunks = [];
    38	  const errChunks = [];
    39	  let currentNow = now;
    40	  let tokenCounter = fencingSeed - 1;
    41	  const defaultAlive = (p, s) => p === pid && s === startTime;
    42	
    43	  const stdout = { write: (s) => { outChunks.push(String(s)); return true; } };
    44	  const stderr = { write: (s) => { errChunks.push(String(s)); return true; } };
    45	
    46	  const execFile = (cmd, args = [], /* opts */ _opts = {}) => {
    47	    const key = [cmd, ...(Array.isArray(args) ? args : [])].join(' ');
    48	    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    49	      if (!(key in execResults)) {
    50	        const e = new Error(`spawn ${cmd} ENOENT`);
    51	        e.code = 'ENOENT';
    52	        return reject(e);
    53	      }
    54	      const r = execResults[key];
    55	      const code = r.code ?? 0;
    56	      const out = r.stdout ?? '';
    57	      const err = r.stderr ?? '';
    58	      if (code !== 0) {
    59	        // util.promisify(execFile) rejects on nonzero exit; error carries code + streams.
    60	        const e = new Error(`Command failed: ${key}`);
    61	        e.code = code;
    62	        e.stdout = out;
    63	        e.stderr = err;
    64	        return reject(e);
    65	      }
    66	      resolve({ stdout: out, stderr: err });
    67	    });
    68	  };
    69	
    70	  return {
    71	    cwd: '/repo',
    72	    env,
    73	    stdin,
    74	    stdout,
    75	    stderr,
    76	    fs,
    77	    execFile,
    78	    now: () => currentNow,
    79	    setNow: (iso) => { currentNow = iso; },
    80	    execPath,
    81	    host,
    82	    pid,
    83	    startTime,
    84	    processAlive: processAlive || defaultAlive,
    85	    // Tiny retry budget: unit tests exercising live-lock refusal stay fast
    86	    // while the retry code path itself still runs (production default: 120x25ms).
    87	    lockRetry: { attempts: 2, delayMs: 2 },
    88	    newFencingToken: () => `tok-${++tokenCounter}`,
    89	    stdoutText: () => outChunks.join(''),
    90	    stderrText: () => errChunks.join(''),
    91	    files: filesSnapshot,
    92	  };
    93	}

    12	// prepare/commit; §Per-module test lists "txn"; plan §Concurrency — the receive

    31	//
    32	// TOKEN BINDING (THE pin). prepare captures a REVISION FINGERPRINT and returns it
    33	//   as an opaque token. It binds every one of these inputs (one rejection test per

    46	//   prepare mutates NOTHING (it cannot persist a "prepared" record — the token is

    49	//   names re-prepare (matches /re-?prepare/i) and performs NO mutation (the

   150	function makeTxnIo({ bundle, journal, configText = CONFIG_TEXT, now = NOW, extra = {} } = {}) {
   151	  const files = {
   152	    [SIG_PATH]: SIG_CONTENT,
   153	    [`${ROOT}/baton.config.json`]: configText,
   154	    [`${ROOT}/.handoff/bundle.json`]: snapText(bundle),
   155	    ...extra,
   156	  };
   157	  if (journal !== undefined) files[`${ROOT}/.handoff/journal.ndjson`] = journal;
   158	  return makeIo({ files, now });
   159	}
